- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap forecast growth to 2–5% per period to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a 1–2% upward bias to forecast to counteract downward drift.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early periods of a 30-day forecast (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply a 2–4% upward adjustment to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and model forecast is flat or declining, assume bullish sentiment is being ignored; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per period to reflect sentiment strength.
